body.target_estimand: The target is \(\tau_P(x_0)\) at a fixed known \(x_0\in[0,1]^d\). Under consistency and conditional exchangeability, \(\tau_P=\mu_{1,P}-\mu_{0,P}\) is a version of \(\mathbb E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X]\); H\"older continuity and exact-uniform full support determine its unique continuous version at every fixed interior or boundary \(x_0\), cf. KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE.
body.estimand_functional: For fixed known \(x_0\in[0,1]^d\), \(\widehat\tau_n(x_0)=\operatorname{clip}_{[-3/4,3/4]}\{v(0)^{\mathsf T}\widetilde Q_n^{-1}\widetilde R_n\}\) on the nonsingular inward-chart branch, with \(R_n\asymp\rho_n=n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta)))}\) for \(S\le S_\star\); at equality this is \(n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\) without a logarithm.

sampling_model.design: The known law \(X\sim\operatorname{Unif}([0,1]^d)\) has exact full support.
sampling_model.units: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent draws from one law \(P\in\mathcal P(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The estimator knows \(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L\) and the uniform design law, but not \(g_P,\mu_{0,P},\tau_P\); it uses deterministic localization and a finite projection correction rather than oracle nuisance inputs.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives a lower bound on a broader bounded-density pointwise CATE class, while Theorem 2 gives an upper bound under additional design and nuisance-estimation conditions; the displayed lower hard laws use separated local support.
Theorem 2.1 bounds the affinity of two convex mixtures of product measures under a measurable partition and coordinate-local perturbations.
Theorems 3--5 establish matched local and global conditional-variance rates under random design using local U-statistics and coupled lower laws.
Theorem 3 and Corollary 4 give local-polynomial R-learner upper rates with deterministic smoothness-dependent tuning under known-density conditions.

body.tldr: For every fixed known \(x_0\in[0,1]^d\), the exact-uniform bounded-overlap Bernoulli model has sharp pointwise CATE risk \(R_n\asymp n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta)))}\) throughout \(S=\alpha+\beta\le d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\). A reflected inward local projection estimator attains the rate on every data set, and a translated correlated-sign component prior proves the genuine fixed-\(n\) same-class converse. At the elbow the rate is exactly \(n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\), with no logarithmic multiplier; strictly below it, nuisance learning causes an unavoidable slower power.

project_justification.gap: The published pointwise CATE theory gives this candidate power on a broader model, but its displayed lower laws delete design mass around nuisance-bump transitions. A lower bound on that broader class does not imply the same bound after fixing \(P_X\) to the exact uniform law, and it does not by itself certify arbitrary boundary or interior point targets on the singleton class.
project_justification.niche: The note isolates the exact known-uniform, bounded-overlap Bernoulli/interiority subclass and proves its pointwise estimation/precision benchmark. The class is a strict subclass of the published general-design model, so a same-class converse is the missing ingredient; identification is already supplied by consistency, exchangeability, overlap, full support, and continuity.
project_justification.fill: A reflected inward chart gives one total finite projection \(U\)-statistic estimator uniformly over fixed \(x_0\). For the converse, a translated compact smooth window and squared frame partition make singleton sign mixtures agree exactly; sparse component factorization, a mixed-amplitude Hellinger bound, and spanning-tree enumeration control the full fixed-\(n\) mixture. At equality, \(n\ell^d\) is a tunably small constant, which closes the elbow without a logarithm.

body.related_work: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE is the closest comparator: its lower theorem covers a broader bounded-density class and its upper theorem requires additional design and nuisance-estimation conditions, whereas the present result closes the fixed-\(n\) converse and matching upper bound on the strict exact-uniform bounded-overlap Bernoulli/interiority subclass. The lower converse therefore transfers upward by subclass inclusion to any broader model that contains this subclass and uses the same point target; the exact-uniform upper proof does not transfer in that direction and is not claimed there. RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009SemiparametricMinimax supplies the product-mixture perspective, but the shared smooth frames here require random overlap-component factorization rather than a deterministic coordinate-local partition. ShenGaoWittenHan2020Variance is a random-design nonlinear-functional analogue for repeated local occupancy. Kennedy2023DRCATE and NieWager2021RLearner provide oracle-facing upper comparisons, while RobinsLiTchetgenVanderVaart2008HOIF motivates the finite projection correction. LiuMukherjeeRobinsTchetgen2021Adaptive studies adaptive nonlinear-functional estimation, whereas the present estimator uses known smoothness. LeeOkuiWhang2017CATEBands studies uniform CATE confidence bands, whereas this note proves pointwise mean-risk only. AtheyWager2021PolicyLearning studies policy-value and regret learning rather than pointwise CATE minimax precision. ChernozhukovWuthrichZhu2021Conformal studies conformal counterfactual and synthetic-control inference rather than this estimand or guarantee. WagerAthey2018CausalForests is an application-facing consumer: this is a precision benchmark for \(\texttt{causal\_forest}\) and R-learner workflows, not a claim that existing forests attain the bound.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The sparse-component summation uses \(n\ell^d\le C\) and therefore certifies only the at-or-below-elbow regime; above the elbow the present prior is not a converse certificate. The finite estimator also uses the known smoothness tuple in its deterministic bandwidth and projection dimension. Constants are not optimized, and the theorem concerns mean absolute pointwise risk rather than a confidence procedure.
body.honest_scope: The proved contribution is the same-class full-support fixed-\(n\) lower bound, paired with a total finite estimator, for every fixed known \(x_0\in[0,1]^d\) and \(S\le S_\star\). It includes boundary points through a reflected inward chart and proves the exact no-log oracle power at \(S=S_\star\). The exact-uniform class is a strict subclass of the published general-design class: only the lower bound transfers upward by subclass inclusion at matching point targets. The note does not claim its upper bound for unknown or nonuniform design, and it does not treat \(\kappa>0\) local overlap decay, adaptive tuning, confidence intervals, integrated loss, or performance guarantees for existing causal forests.
